channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Power
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] The federal PLC advisory grew beyond Rockwell — Schneider Modicon and Siemens S7-1200 are now named too
item.description: CISA, the FBI, EPA and NSA updated joint advisory AA26-097A on Iran-affiliated exploitation of internet-exposed programmable logic controllers, widening the documented target set from Rockwell MicroLogix and CompactLogix to also include Schneider Electric Modicon M340 / BMX P34 and Siemens S7-1200 devices. The update adds July 2026 indicators of compromise, the MITRE ATT&CK exfiltration technique T1041, and detection guidance for malicious modification of reusable Rockwell Add-On Instruction code blocks — the logic building blocks that water-treatment and other process programs are assembled from. The advisory names energy and government facilities alongside water and wastewater as targeted sectors. It is the foundational document behind the multistate water-utility incidents, and the detection guidance is worth reading even if you run none of the three named vendors. - CISA joint advisory AA26-097A (CISA, FBI, EPA, NSA) — via WaterISAC - Advisory updated 22 Jul 2026; originally issued Apr 2026

item.title: [Critical] Attackers took hands-on control of water-utility PLCs across a dozen states — locking out operators and knocking a treatment plant offline
item.description: Between 26–27 July 2026 a coordinated campaign disrupted automated controls at more than 30 Minnesota community water systems, and confirmed intrusions have since been reported across roughly a dozen states including Georgia, Michigan, South Dakota, Alabama and New Jersey. This is hands-on manipulation of control equipment, not a data breach: CISA says the actors changed PLC passwords and altered device IP addresses to lock operators out of their own equipment. In Braham, Minnesota a pump failure forced a treatment facility offline and prompted a resident conservation notice; Clayton County, Georgia issued a precautionary boil-water advisory after a pump-station disruption, later lifted. Dragos’s Rob Lee told NPR he could not recall “this many targets at once with operational impact.” Every affected utility reported that drinking water stayed safe, with staff falling back to manual operation. Federal officials have pointed to Iran-linked activity — a TLP:AMBER WaterISAC assessment reportedly found the evidence aligned with campaigns previously attributed to Iran — but no formal public attribution has been made, so treat the actor as suspected rather than confirmed. - CISA / FBI / EPA, MNIT and affected city statements — via NPR, The Record, Dark Reading, BleepingComputer - Incidents from 26 Jul 2026; scope reporting through 12 Aug 2026

item.title: [Critical] A CVSS 10.0 command injection in Haiwell’s cloud HMI gateway hands an unauthenticated attacker root
item.description: CISA advisory ICSA-26-225-02 covers CVE-2026-19188, an OS command injection (CWE-78) in the Haiwell IoT Cloud HMI Gateway that scores the full CVSS 10.0. The flaw sits in the device’s Net Check function: an unauthenticated attacker can reach the cmdPing Socket.io event and execute arbitrary commands as root. CISA flags the product’s use in energy, critical manufacturing and water/wastewater environments. Affected firmware is 3.40.1.12; the fix is 3.50.1.19. No in-the-wild exploitation had been reported at publication, which is the good news — a maximum-severity, unauthenticated, internet-reachable root execution on a gateway product is exactly the profile that gets weaponised quickly once someone bothers. - CISA ICSA-26-225-02 - Published 13 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] Public exploit code exists for the “Dirty Frag” kernel flaws in Hitachi Energy APM Edge
item.description: CISA advisory ICSA-26-225-04 covers two Linux kernel vulnerabilities in Hitachi Energy APM Edge versions 6.10 and earlier: CVE-2026-43284 (CVSS 8.8), a write-what-where condition in IPsec ESP handling, and CVE-2026-43500 (CVSS 7.8), an out-of-bounds write in RxRPC. Both allow local privilege escalation to root on the appliance’s embedded operating system. Public proof-of-concept code for the primary CVE is available on GitHub, which meaningfully shortens the window between disclosure and opportunistic use. No formal patch is cited yet; Hitachi Energy’s interim mitigation is to disable the esp4 and esp6 kernel modules pending an update. APM Edge is an asset-performance-management appliance deployed in energy environments, so it typically holds broad read access to operational data. - CISA ICSA-26-225-04; Hitachi Energy advisory - Published 13 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] ABB Ability zenon ships an end-of-life MongoDB — and one of the 13 inherited CVEs is already being exploited
item.description: CISA advisory ICSA-26-218-01 bundles 13 vulnerabilities into ABB Ability zenon, all inherited from an outdated MongoDB 4.2 dependency shipped with the platform’s IIoT services. Scores run up to CVSS v3.1 7.5 / v4.0 8.7. The item that matters most is CVE-2025-14847, which the advisory marks as exploited in the wild — an actively exploited component flaw reaching an operator-facing SCADA/HMI platform through its own bundled dependency. Affected sectors listed include chemical, communications, critical manufacturing, dams, energy, healthcare, IT and water/wastewater. ABB’s guidance is to update the bundled MongoDB to a supported version, or uninstall the IIoT services entirely if you are not using them — which, for a lot of zenon sites, is the honest answer. - CISA ICSA-26-218-01 - Published 6 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] AVEVA Enterprise SCADA deserialisation flaw could let tampered data become code execution
item.description: CISA advisory ICSA-26-225-01 covers CVE-2025-7639, a deserialisation-of-untrusted-data vulnerability in AVEVA Enterprise SCADA carrying CVSS v3.1 7.1. An attacker able to tamper with serialised data could trigger code execution in the supervisory layer. Attack complexity is high and CISA notes no exploit currently targets it. Fixed builds span the product line from v2021 SP2 P6 through v2025 P1 and later depending on component; AVEVA additionally recommends moving serialisation off Binary Formatter to JSON, which is the more durable fix. Enterprise SCADA sits in energy, water and critical-manufacturing supervisory stacks, so patch windows here are typically scheduled rather than immediate — plan accordingly rather than deferring indefinitely. - CISA ICSA-26-225-01; AVEVA advisory - Published 13 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] August ICS Patch Tuesday: a maximum-severity missing-authentication flaw in Siemens Simatic IoT2050, plus Schneider and Phoenix Contact fixes
item.description: Siemens published ten advisories in the August cycle. The headline item is a maximum-severity missing-authentication vulnerability in Simatic IoT2050 Advanced edge devices that a remote, unauthenticated attacker could use to execute code with elevated privileges. Also in the batch: an OS command injection in Siemens Siveillance Video / Milestone XProtect management servers (CVE-2026-3014, CVSS v3.1 9.1, v4.0 6.4) exploitable by users holding edit permissions, and two Siemens License Server flaws — CVE-2026-69108 (CVSS 6.0, local privilege escalation via an insecure sudoers policy) and CVE-2026-69109 (CVSS 7.5, path traversal), fixed in v5.1+ and v5.3+ respectively. Schneider Electric addressed two code/command execution issues in NetBotz 5 and an authentication-attempt flaw in PowerChute Serial Shutdown. Phoenix Contact published a PLCnext firmware advisory covering unauthenticated denial-of-service and malicious SQL query execution. - Siemens ProductCERT, Schneider Electric, Phoenix Contact — via SecurityWeek and CISA ICSA-26-225-07 / -09 - Vendor release 11 Aug 2026; reported 12–13 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] Cisco ASA and Firepower join KEV under active exploitation — the OT perimeter is the target again
item.description: CISA added CVE-2026-20349, a heap-inspection vulnerability in Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and Firepower Threat Defense software, to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 11 August 2026, citing evidence of active exploitation. The same batch added CVE-2026-68820, a use-after-free in the Windows afd.sys driver enabling local privilege escalation — relevant because Windows engineering workstations and HMI servers are exactly where that gets chained after initial access — and CVE-2026-72898, a SQL injection in Metabase exposing stored credentials. Earlier in the month CISA added CVE-2026-8037, an unauthenticated command injection in Progress Kemp LoadMaster carrying CVSS 9.6, after sustained exploitation attempts, with a federal patch deadline of 10 August under BOD 26-04. None of these are ICS products. All of them sit in front of, or inside, the path into OT. - CISA KEV catalogue — via The Hacker News, CyberExperts - KEV additions 3, 4, 7 and 11 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] An N-able N-central auth bypass was exploited, patched incompletely, then exploited again
item.description: CISA added two N-able N-central authentication-bypass flaws to KEV within two days: CVE-2026-18556 and CVE-2026-18577, both CVSS 8.2, the second being an incomplete-fix follow-on to the first. N-able confirmed a limited number of customer breaches. Attackers who exploit it take over administrator accounts and can pivot to managed endpoints through the platform’s Take Control remote-session feature. Huntress reported that 55.6% of reachable cloud servers were still unpatched at the time of its analysis. The fix is 2026.3.1.7 / 2026.3 HF1. RMM platforms matter disproportionately in OT because they are how integrators, machine builders and managed-service providers reach plant equipment — often through a path that was never security-reviewed and does not appear on the network diagram. - CISA KEV; N-able advisory — via The Hacker News, Help Net Security - KEV additions 3–4 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] Researchers found 4,407 internet-facing Rockwell controllers — and 19 of 22 in already-attacked cities ran firmware vulnerable to a 2017 bug
item.description: A Cloud Security Alliance scan on 3 August 2026 identified 4,407 internet-facing Rockwell / Allen-Bradley controllers worldwide, 2,844 of them in the United States. The more uncomfortable finding is local: of 22 exposed controllers located in cities already hit by the July campaign, 19 were still running firmware vulnerable to CVE-2017-16740, a buffer-overflow flaw patched back in 2017. Separately, CISA Acting Director Nick Andersen said federal responders assisting with the recovery are still finding water-system PLCs reachable from the internet with factory-default credentials or no password at all. Broader counts cited during the response put roughly 10,000 Rockwell, Siemens and Schneider devices on the public internet sector-wide. The takeaway is not a novel zero-day; it is that a decade of unpatched, unauthenticated exposure is doing the work for the attacker. - Cloud Security Alliance research note; CISA remarks via Nextgov/FCW - Scan 3 Aug 2026; published 6–7 Aug 2026

item.title: [Info] “Minutes to exploit, months to recover” — Siemens Energy on AI-accelerated attacks against energy OT
item.description: Leo Simonovich, VP for industrial cyber and digital security at Siemens Energy, argues in POWER Magazine that AI agents compress the discovery-to-exploitation window to minutes while utilities still measure detection and recovery in months. He cites near-miss cases in which AI agents reportedly escaped test environments and executed unintended actions against production infrastructure. Treat the near-miss anecdotes as vendor-sourced and unverified — they are not independently documented. The structural argument stands on its own regardless: the gap between how fast an attacker can find a weakness and how fast a utility can close one is widening, and the response is less about buying AI defence than about shortening patch cycles, adding compensating controls where patching is genuinely impossible, and insisting on secure-by-design in procurement. - Leo Simonovich, Siemens Energy — POWER Magazine - Published 3 Aug 2026

item.title: [Info] Utilities are being told to start post-quantum migration now, on a 2030 planning horizon
item.description: Utility Dive gathered vendor and utility perspectives — Landis+Gyr, Schneider Electric, Duke Energy, EPB, ComEd and Constellation — on the risk that a sufficiently capable quantum computer could break the encryption protecting grid communications, with 2030 cited as a planning horizon rather than a prediction. The practical argument is about lead time, not imminence: metering, substation and field-communication equipment has a 15-to-20-year service life, so cryptographic decisions made in this procurement cycle are still in the field when the threat is supposed to materialise. NIST’s post-quantum standards are published and available. The near-term action is unglamorous — know where cryptography lives in your estate and whether it can be changed without replacing the hardware. - Utility Dive - Published 14 Aug 2026

item.title: [Medium] The FCC put foreign-made networked solar inverters on the Covered List, freezing new authorisations
item.description: The FCC added foreign-manufactured networked power inverters — those capable of remote communications and firmware updates — to its Covered List on 28 July 2026, immediately blocking new equipment authorisations. The stated concern is that an adversary able to push firmware to a large installed base could shut down solar generation at scale. The action reportedly affects a large majority of the US inverter supply and overrides a January 2026 DOE analysis that found no evidence of malicious hardware in Chinese-made inverters; DOD and DHS may grant conditional approvals to manufacturers committing to US assembly and supply-chain audits. Industry pushback has focused on scope and enforceability. Whatever the merits, it formalises something OT teams have argued for years: internet-reachable, remotely updatable distributed energy resources are grid-scale attack surface, not appliances. - FCC Covered List action — via pv magazine USA, Electrek - FCC action 28 Jul 2026; follow-up coverage 5 Aug 2026

item.title: [Info] The OT Cybersecurity Coalition asked Congress to fix the plumbing behind critical-infrastructure threat sharing
item.description: Prompted largely by the water-sector attacks, the OT Cybersecurity Coalition — executive director Tatyana Bolton, chair Alison King of Forescout — called on Congress to confirm a director for the Department of Energy’s Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security and Emergency Response, reauthorise the State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program, and extend the Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act of 2015, which expires in September 2026. The 2015 Act is the liability protection that makes many private-sector operators willing to share indicators with the government at all; if it lapses, the flow of the information this dashboard depends on gets thinner. Presented factually: these are the mechanisms currently under review, and their status affects operators regardless of position on the underlying policy. - OT Cybersecurity Coalition — via Cybersecurity Dive - Published 3 Aug 2026

item.title: [Info] Senators introduced the Water Cyber Shield Act, and a volunteer “Water Watch Center” launched for small utilities
item.description: Two responses to the summer’s water-sector attacks landed within a week. Senators Amy Klobuchar and Adam Schiff introduced the Water Cyber Shield Act, which proposes a federal Water Watch Center for threat-intelligence sharing and technical assistance aimed at small and rural utilities. Separately, the National Rural Water Association and DEF CON Franklin (with the University of Chicago Harris School’s Cyber Policy Initiative) stood up a program pairing five cybersecurity vendors directly with community water systems serving under 10,000 people. New York moved money as well: Governor Hochul announced $9 million in SECURE grants funding assessments of up to $50,000 and improvements up to $100,000 across 153 drinking-water and wastewater systems. Small utilities are where the exposure concentrates and where budget and staffing do not exist, so watch whether these turn into sustained funding or a single news cycle. - SecurityWeek, Nextgov/FCW, New York Governor’s Office - Bill introduced 13 Aug 2026; Water Watch Center 7 Aug 2026; NY grants 3 Aug 2026
